item: E1 latch: a first failed read pauses at once and is read again by itself; a table that fails again after a clean read stays paused
key_paths: src/database/damage.py; src/database/verify.py; tests/test_damage_reread.py; tests/conftest.py; tests/test_database_damage.py; src/static/locales/*.json
summary: A corruption error met while the app runs still latches its file at once; the registry now claims, in the same lock block, a re-read of the tables the failing statement writes (identifier words intersected with the file's tables, FTS shadow tables with the virtual table) and verify.reread reads each on a fresh read-only connection through check_table (two reads where one says damaged, R100). Every table clean ends the pause by itself and the record says reread: clean; damaged, unread, no statement, a switch, a stop, a failure, a running check or a missing file keep the latch exactly as a first failed read leaves it, with the fixed reason in the record. A table released this way that fails again in the same process latches and stays (reread: stayed); a failed read during the re-read holds the latch; a start during it does not release; a replaced file drops the late answer. note_raw_driver_error now latches for a closed Connection. Two strings x12. The registry's rereads attribute is on for the process's own registry, off for one a caller builds, and off for the suite's global one. 44 new tests on real files; 33 mutants of the new code killed (three survived the first run and have a test each); the independent read's 1 block and 6 medium findings are folded in. Not measured: the cost of the re-read of a big table on the users' stores; how often a code 11 does not repeat in the field.
